If everything goes according to plan, and I think the Judges will have less questions to ask, we should be finished with the cross-examination on Wednesday, or finished with the witness on Wednesday, because on Thursday we have another witness scheduled, which means we have eight hours left, and that means four hours tomorrow, four hours Wednesday, which will give the Defence eight hours in total, and that should be enough to complete the examination of this witness. Now, since we have a few minutes left, I'd like to give the oral ruling that I promised, and I'd like to ask the Prosecution to listen carefully. The title of the oral decision concerns the Prosecution motion on admission of evidence relating to Christopher Beese's testimony. The date is the 25th of August, 2006. The Prosecution filed a motion concerning the admission of documents concerning Mr. Beese's testimony. In its motion, the Prosecution requested the admission of 383 documents from the ECMM. With this regard, the Prosecution provided an annex and communicated confidentially a chart for each of the documents they were requesting to be admitted, and different conditions were mentioned relating to the Chamber's decision concerning admission -- admissibility of evidence. The date concerned was the 13th of July, 2006. The Trial Chamber, nevertheless, notes that the Prosecution's motion does not fully comply with the criteria requested in paragraph 6 of the decision referred to. One, the motion does not describe the indicia of reliability for each of the documents that they want to have admitted into evidence. The Trial Chamber believes that this information is all the more relevant in that ECMM is not the origin of some of the documents that the Prosecution wants to have admitted into evidence. Two, the motion does not contain references for some of the documents. It doesn't contain reference to the relevant paragraphs in the indictment. Three, the motion doesn't mention the reasons for which the documents that the Prosecution wants to have admitted into evidence could not be presented to some other witness and not to Mr. Beese. In this respect, the Trial Chamber concludes that most of the documents that the Prosecution wants to have admitted into evidence under paragraph 5 of the Prosecution's motion seem to be such that they could be introduced through other witnesses. Four, the motion doesn't mention the reasons for which the documents are indispensable for a fair determination of the matter. The Chamber insists on the fact that the decision of the 13th of July, 2006, and the guidelines concerning the admission of evidence that accompanies this decision are definitive and must be respected to the letter. Since the parties haven't appealed against this decision, it's the Trial Chamber's responsibility to rule. The Chamber, therefore, believes that the information provided in the Prosecution's submissions on Friday, on last Friday, is not complete. The Chamber invites the Prosecution to complete its motion in the light of the decision dated the 13th of July, 2006, and in the light of the explanations provided and within 10 days, the 10-day deadline mentioned in the decision. This should, therefore, be before the 1st of September, 2006, failing which the motion will be definitively rejected. This is what I mentioned to you earlier on at the beginning of the hearing. Mr. Scott, it's necessary to sit down and respond to the four points I have made by the 1st of September. It's almost time to conclude now. We'll see each other tomorrow at 9.00. In the meantime, you shouldn't meet anyone. I see that Mr. Murphy is on his feet now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Mr. President, as far as the Defence response to the Prosecution motion is concerned, may I take it that the time for that response will run from the date when the Prosecution submits an amended motion in accordance with your ruling?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Obviously, because you have to state what your position is with regard to the four points I mentioned. So that is quite logical. I didn't mention that because it seemed to be self- evident to me. There's something that Mr. Prlic would like to say.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have a request to make, but I could make the request tomorrow morning. Just two minutes, but I can do that tomorrow morning, because I see we've almost finish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. We still have a few more minutes, so please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's about our work programme, our schedule. I have looked at the name of the witness coming in on Monday. He is my colleague, a historian from the 19th century, and - - or, rather, this next witness will testify for nine hours. But looking at the proofing chart, apart from the joint criminal enterprise and the rest of it, the object is to look at 801 mentions made -- mention is made of my name, paragraphs 2, 3, 17.1. It is my position that in general terms, all this can be dealt with in an hour or two of examination. However, bearing in mind the fact that the indictment reads as it stands, that it has been confirmed and that we have a decision according to which this gentleman is being introduced as an expert witness, we consider that each of these allegations, 801, must be dealt with during the cross-examination. Of course, some of them are linked to the same documents of the 457 that are going to be tendered. But if there are additional documents added to that number, then we consider that the minimum amount of time, if we accord three minutes to each one of those 800 mentions, is 3.400 minutes or exactly ten working days just for my own Defence counsel. So I'd like to have a ruling from you, a suitable ruling and one which will ensure that my rights are respected in this trial or to give us some other guidelines. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We listened to what you have said. It's 7.00 p.m. now, so the Judges will examine the issue you have raised, and there will be a decision with regard to your motion, with regard to your request. But at this point in time, Mr. Scott, would you like to make a response given that Mr. Prlic has evoked a number of issues, the duration of the examination-in-chief, the cross-examination? He has also mentioned 800-odd documents -- 800-odd references that concern Mr. Prlic, the documents that you want to present, and if we spend two minutes on each document, Mr. Prlic says we'd need over 3.000 minutes to reach -- for the hearing. Is there anything you'd like to say about this at the moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We have all night to think about this. I'm not sure whether you will be examining this witness or one of your colleagues. But Mr. Prlic, rest assured that the Judges will examine your request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I think for the record and to be precise, it would be correct if you would tell the name of the witness you are talking about. I think you have not mentioned him.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I didn't mention the name. This is Mr. Tomljanovich.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I guessed so, but thank you for telling us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is several minutes after 7.00. I wish you a very pleasant evening, and we reconvene tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 29th day of August, 2006, at 9.00 a.m.
